rule: A local bound directly to a function literal (`const f = () => ...`, `local function f`, ...) is a named nested function: ID `outer.f` (Python form), and calls to it are high. Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function (or the module/type at top level). | Lua: ... local functions `mod.f` / `outer.f`; module-level code's caller is the module.
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. `local cube = function` (top level) is the named function `geom.cube`; `local half = function` inside `geom#area` is `geom#area.half` (Python form `pkg.mod.C#m.inner`). The comparator passed to table.sort is anonymous: its two `cube` calls (line 19, two edges) fold into `geom#area`. The anonymous function passed to pcall in main.lua is at top level, so its `geom.area` call folds into the module `main`. `M.unit = square(1)` is module-level code: caller `geom`.
